senses.definition_en: God forbid

examples.english:
"Quiet, you blasphemer!...Are you really comparing this house of prostitution and crime to the very domus Dei [house of God]"?
"God forbid such evilness, Father […] !"
examples.ref: 1870, Vicente Fidel López, La novia del hereje o la Inquisición de Lima:
examples.text:
-¡Calla, blasfemo!... ¿conque comparas a esa casa de prostitución y de crimen con la que es domus Dei?
-¡Dios me libre de tal maldad, Padre[…]!
examples.translation:
"Quiet, you blasphemer!...Are you really comparing this house of prostitution and crime to the very domus Dei [house of God]"?
"God forbid such evilness, Father […] !"

examples.english:
"Are you throwing me out?"
"No", I defended, "I'm not throwing you out, no! God forbid! If you want I'll go and you stay here, so you know I'm not throwing you out."
examples.text:
¿Me echa usted?
–No, me defiendo. ¡No te echo, no! ¡Dios me libre! Si quieres me ire yo y te quedas aquí tú, para que veas que no te echo.
examples.translation:
"Are you throwing me out?"
"No", I defended, "I'm not throwing you out, no! God forbid! If you want I'll go and you stay here, so you know I'm not throwing you out."

examples.english: But if my mum finds out that she's known something and I haven't, God forbid! Imagine what she's going to tell me!
examples.ref: 1986, María Luisa de Luján Campos, Para que me lo guardes en secreto:
examples.text: Pero si se entera mi mamá de que ella ha sabido algo y yo no, Dios me libre, ¡qué cosas va a decirme!
examples.translation: But if my mum finds out that she's known something and I haven't, God forbid! Imagine what she's going to tell me!

examples.english:
"Oh! Would you be so kind as to stop using "Ma'am" with me, it makes me seem old", said the lady, in a smiling face, while looking at Vince
"Of course. God forbid I should use it again."
examples.text:
¡Ah!, y si tiene inconveniente, quíteme lo de “doña” que hace muy vieja —dijo la señora, con rostro riente, mientras miraba a Vince.
 —Claro, Dios me libre de repetirlo.
examples.translation:
"Oh! Would you be so kind as to stop using "Ma'am" with me, it makes me seem old", said the lady, in a smiling face, while looking at Vince
"Of course. God forbid I should use it again."

senses.definition_en: seafood shop, especially one that specializes in shellfish

examples.english: I buy my seafood at the Mercado Central, at the seafood shop Los Pochos. They have everything: salmon, swordfish, congers. At home I cut them up myself and freeze them in pieces so it will be easier to cook them later.
examples.ref: 2012 March 7, “Marcial Tagle con delantal [Marcial Tagle with an apron]”, in La Tercera:
examples.text: Compro los pescados en el Mercado Central, en la marisquería Los Pochos. Tienen de todo: salmones, albacoras, congrios. En la casa los trozo yo mismo y los congelo por porciones para que sea más fácil cocinarlos después.
examples.translation: I buy my seafood at the Mercado Central, at the seafood shop Los Pochos. They have everything: salmon, swordfish, congers. At home I cut them up myself and freeze them in pieces so it will be easier to cook them later.

glosses: seafood shop, especially one that specializes in shellfish

senses.definition_en: seafood restaurant, especially one that specializes in shellfish

examples.english: With a nostalgic aesthetic of ports and wise fishermen, the seafood restaurant Don José stands out as one of the best places to eat marine delicacies in Zona Norte. The manner is welcoming and the atmosphere rowdy. Shellfish are, of course, the star of the menu.
examples.ref: 2011 February 8, Cecilia Acuña, “Los mejores restaurantes para comer pescado en Buenos Aires [The best restaurants to eat seafood in Buenos Aires]”, in La Nación (Argentina):
examples.text: Con una estética nostálgica de puertos y pescadores sabios, la marisquería Don José se destaca como uno de los mejores lugares para comer delicias marinas de Zona Norte. El trato es acogedor y el ambiente alborotado. Los mariscos, por supuesto, son los protagonistas de la carta.
examples.translation: With a nostalgic aesthetic of ports and wise fishermen, the seafood restaurant Don José stands out as one of the best places to eat marine delicacies in Zona Norte. The manner is welcoming and the atmosphere rowdy. Shellfish are, of course, the star of the menu.

glosses: seafood restaurant, especially one that specializes in shellfish
